newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian communist chief says trial political.
newsitem.headline: Albanian communist chief says trial political.

text.p: Albania's last communist president Ramiz Alia, awaiting trial on charges of genocide and crimes against humanity, ws quoted on Tuesday as saying his arrest was politically motivated.
In a letter delivered to an opposition Socialist newspaper by his son-in-law, Alia said he considered himself a political prisoner and the charges against him as anti-nationalistic.
"It is clear to anyone I am a political prisoner and being tried as an opponent of the current regime," his letter said.
He said his trial was intended to "distract attention from the political and economic problems concerning the country".

In the past week Albania has been hit by waves of protests against the government, blamed by many for the collapse of pyramid investment schemes in which hundreds of people have lost their life savings.

If found guilty, Alia -- the successor of Stalinist dictator Enver Hoxha -- could face a sentence ranging from 15 years jail to the death penalty. He has been detained since his arrest in February last year.

Alia, president until 1992 when the opposition Democratic Party won a landslide victory in general elections, is due to be tried together with two former interior ministers, at a date still to be fixed.

Around 100,000 Albanians are believed to have been forced into exile in remote villages during 45 years of communist rule because of their opposition to the Stalinist government or for trying to escape from the isolated Balkan country.

A controversial "genocide" law was passed in 1995, so called because the government claims the communists tried to eradicate a whole section of society -- dissidents. Albania has so far tried 33 former communists on the charge of genocide.
Western governments have expressed concern over the law, which also bans former communist officials from standing for posts in politics, the judiciary and the media until 2002.
